summary.one_liner: Devon is an open-source AI pair programmer that runs as a Python agent backend with a Node-based web UI (Electron-style) or terminal UI for editing and exploring codebases.
summary.what_it_does: Devon is an interactive coding agent that works on files in the directory where it is started, and it can be steered or corrected while it runs. The README lists features including multi-file editing, codebase exploration, config writing, test writing, bug fixing, and architecture exploration. It supports hosted models via Anthropic, OpenAI, and Groq API keys, and a local mode using Ollama with deepseek-coder, which the README says is immature. Installation is through pipx (backend package devon_agent) plus npx devon-ui for the UI, or npm for the devon-tui terminal interface. Telemetry on event types and failures is collected unless the DEVON_TELEMETRY_DISABLED variable is set to true.
use_cases: running a coding agent from the terminal
notable: Interactive agent that can be corrected mid-task, with access limited to the starting directory
Separate backend (devon_agent) and UI options: Electron-style web UI via npx devon-ui or terminal UI via devon-tui
Supports Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o, and Groq llama3-70b per the README's model checklist
Local model mode via Ollama, with explicit warnings about maturity
Community-driven development with a Discord and a CONTRIBUTING.md file
caveats: README says Windows support is in progress and not yet available
Local model mode is described as not mature and likely to perform much worse than hosted models
Minimal functionality for non-Python languages, and sometimes requires specifying the target file
Project describes itself as super early
keywords: let an ai edit my project files
ai help fixing bugs in my code
